title: Longest Crawl
story: A cave is a tree of chambers: from the entrance chamber, each chamber leads to at most two deeper ones, one on the left and one on the right, and every chamber has its own number. A caver wants the longest crawl in the cave: a route between any two chambers that never passes through a chamber twice. Report how many tunnels it uses. The longest crawl need not pass through the entrance. An empty cave or a single chamber gives 0.

notes: The cave can be as deep as it has chambers.

hints: For one chamber, the longest crawl that turns around in it goes as deep as it can on the left and as deep as it can on the right. The answer is the best such crawl over all chambers.

So every chamber must know how deep its branches go, which means children are handled before their parents. POP chambers from one stack and PUSH each onto a second stack: emptying the second stack later gives every child before its parent.

Keep a map from a chamber's NODE VALUE to its depth. For each chamber from the second stack: GET the depths of its LEFT and RIGHT chambers (0 for NOTHING), update the best with their sum, and PUT 1 PLUS the larger one for this chamber.
edgeCases: the longest crawl does not pass through the entrance
a cave that is one long passage
